caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 203 of 1985.
lawyer:
Mr. Gour Gopal Shaha, Advocate ----- For the Appellants. 
No one ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Hazera Khatun & ors ----- Appellants  
Vs. 
Amulya Chandra Chaklader & ors ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mohammad Ismailuddin Sarker J: This appeal by the appellants who are the heirs of the original plaintiff No. 1, is directed against the order dated 16.4.85 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Case No. 91 of 1984 dismissing their application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the order dated 3.11.82 dismissing OC Suit No. 306 of 1981 for default. 

 4. Thereafter on 25.9.84 the appellants who are widow and sons respectively of late Akram Hossain filed an application under Order 9 rule 9 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the order of dismissal of the suit for default dated 3.11.82 This application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 91 of 1984. 

 5. It is stated in the application that during the pendency of the suit plaintiff No. 1 Akram Hossain died on 7.4.82 leaving behind the appellant No. 1, his widow and 3 minor sons; that the appellants did not know anything about the suit and came to learn on 23.9.84 that the suit was dismissed for default on 3.11.82; that the plaintiff No. 1 Akram Hossain was killed by miscreants and since appellant No. 1 is a pardanashin lady and the other appellants are minors they had no knowledge of the suit and coming to know about the dismissal of the suit for default, they filed the application with a prayer for condonation of delay. 

 6. At the trial the appellant No. 1 Hazera Khatun examined herself as PW 1 in support of their case but the learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned order dated 16.4.85 dismissed the Miscellaneous Case as net maintainable simply stating as follows :— 

 "It is an admitted fact that present petitioner was not party in original suit, Further she was not substituted on death of her husband who was one of the plaintiffs. In view of the circumstances it is found that the Miscellaneous Case in the present form is not maintainable and as such it fails." 

 7. It is submitted by Mr. Gour Gopal Shaha, the learned Advocate for the appellants, that OC Suit No. 306 of 1981 was dismissed for default on 3.11.82 when the appellants predecessor-in-interest Akram Hossain, plaintiff No. 1, was alive and there was no occasion for the appellants to be substituted in the suit and as such the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in rejecting the application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure as not maintainable. The learned Advocate further submitted that the appellants claiming through the said Akram Hossain after his death have filed the Miscellaneous Case for setting aside the order of dismissal of the suit for default and as such the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in rejecting their application on the ground that they were not parties in the original suit. The learned Advocate also submitted that in view of the provision of section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure the learned Subordinate Judge should have held that the application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure was maintainable at the instance of the appellant-petitioners. 

 8. It appears that the suit was dismissed for de-fault on 3.11.82 and before that the plaintiff No. 1 died. The appellants being the heirs of plaintiff No. 1 filed the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 9 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a prayer for condonation of delay. The learned Subordinate Judge without entering into the merits of the application dismissed the Miscellaneous Case on the ground that the appellants were not parties in the original suit nor they have been substituted on the death of the plaintiff No. 1. 

 11. There was no such provision as the present section 146 in the Code of Civil Procedure of 1882. That is why there was difference of opinions on the question whether the legal representatives of a deceased defendant could apply to set aside an ex parte decree under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code. The High Court of Calcutta held that he could, in the case of Ganoda Vs. Shib Narain (ILR 29 Cal 33). On the other hand, the High Court of Madras in the case of Sambasiv Vs. Veera (ILR 28 Mad 361) held that he could not; the Allahabad High Court also held that he could not, in the case of Janki Vs. Sukrani (ILR 21 All 274). This controversy has been set at rest by introducing section 146 in the Code of Civil Procedure of 1908 with the object of facilitating the exercise of rights by persons in whom they come to be vested by devolution or assignment. 

 12. Section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure was considered and interpreted by the Supreme Court of India in the case of Smf. Saila Bala Dassi Vs. Nirmala Sundari Dassi reported in AIR 1958(SC) 394 equal to 1958 SCR 1287 wherein their Lord-ships held as follows: 

 13. In the instant case the appellants are no other persons than the legal representatives of the deceased plaintiff No.1 who died after the dismissal of the suit. It is true that the appellants could have filed an application for substitution to be substituted in place of the deceased plaintiff No. 1 during the pendency of the suit; but after the dismissal of the suit there is no occasion for the appellants to file any application for substitution. But they being the heirs of the deceased plaintiff can file an application for setting aside the order of dismissal of the suit for default and section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that where any proceedings may be taken or application made by or against any person then the proceedings may be taken and the application may be made by or against any person claiming under him. Obviously the suit having been dismissed for default, plaintiff No.1 while alive could have filed an application for setting aside the order of dismissal of the suit. 

 14. The appellants claiming under plaintiff No. 1 after his death therefore, can also apply for setting aside the order of dismissal of the suit under Order 9, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In that view of the matter the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in holding that the Miscellaneous Case was not maintainable. 

 15. For the foregoing reasons this Appeal is allowed. The impugned order dated 16.4.85 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is set aside and the learned Subordinate Judge is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 91 of 1984 on merit. Since nobody appeared on behalf of the respondents there will be no order as to costs.
